clue.text: Losing Head of Recruitment employed in Surrey town

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter drops out of the word

parts.note: someone employed is in work, or working

indicators.note: the head of anything is its top, so only the opening letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of the word, which is the one to remove

explanation.surface: A firm in a commuter town loses the person who runs its hiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals on Head of Recruitment are for show. WORKING without its R leaves WOKING, a commuter town in Surrey, a county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Woking is a large commuter settlement in that English county, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Not all cadets awkwardly turned up drunk

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning letters upwards makes them read from the bottom to the top
only part of the run of words is used, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: six consecutive letters spanning the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Clumsy cadets stagger in from a night out the worse for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters are hidden: caDETS AWkwardly, read upwards, gives WASTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is common slang for very intoxicated, a close synonym of the adjective used here.

clue.text: Clever clogs Kelvin will not fancy defending answer

parts.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so one piece is put around another
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
A is the usual abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A smug clever person named Kelvin refuses to like the reply he is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will not fancy' reads as refusing to like something, but 'fancy' rearranges WILL NOT around A, all after K. Clever clogs is a British phrase for a show-off who thinks they know everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe a person who parades their supposed knowledge, so they are informal synonyms.

clue.text: Developing perfume after snag is discovered

indicators.note: the piece named first goes behind the piece named second, reversing the clue's order
to dis-cover is to take off the covering, so the outside letters are stripped and the middle kept

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
a perfume is a scent

explanation.surface: A new fragrance in development runs into a problem when its secret leaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' suggests finding something out; here it means uncovered, so snag loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into being and beginning to grow, which matches developing as an adjective.

clue.text: Defamatory speech by one resident of Anglesey?

indicators.note: beside means placed next to, here at the front, so the piece named second leads

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
spoken defamation is the legal term for it

explanation.surface: Someone from a Welsh island is accused of saying damaging things about another.
explanation.walkthrough: Anglesey is an island off the north-west coast of Wales; the question mark flags that its resident is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone living on an island is an islander, and Anglesey is one, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Stall displaying seafood that's rather cold

parts.note: a market stall is a stand
a stall displaying goods is a stand of them
fish is the main kind of seafood

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's display at the market is kept chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests chilled seafood, but 'cold' describes a manner, not a temperature; 'displaying' is a loose stand-in for OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A standoffish person is distant and unfriendly, which is what a cold manner means.

clue.text: Takes for granted Number 10 shortly will have reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle reorganises a set of members, so the letters are put in a new order
made short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the answer to the clue numbered 10 in this grid

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister, at Number 10 Downing Street, will soon reorganise the Cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 looks like Downing Street but points to 10 across, MASSEUSE. Cut short to MASSEUS, its letters rearrange into ASSUMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume something is to accept it as true without proof, so the verbs are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Old priest completed enthralling game

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: did is to have completed a task
RU is rugby union, the standard crossword game

explanation.surface: An elderly clergyman finished a game that had him gripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' reads as describing the game, but it tells you DID holds RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Druids were the priestly class of the ancient Celts, so an old priest is a fair description.

clue.text: White wine Sir Nigel ordered

indicators.note: put into order, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A titled diner asks for a glass of white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like requesting a drink; it actually reorders the letters of SIR NIGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a grape variety and the white wine made from it, typical of Germany and Alsace.

clue.text: Wife maybe put pickle over pizza originally

indicators.note: something put over another covers it, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to souse is to pickle in brine or vinegar

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its beginning, so its opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wife puts pickle on top of a pizza.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUSE goes over P. 'maybe' marks the definition as an example: a wife is one kind of spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife is one example of a marriage partner; the qualifier makes the example fair for the general term.

clue.text: Spain blocks widespread employment producing rubber

indicators.note: a block stands in the way, so one piece sits inside another and obstructs it

parts.note: mass as an adjective means large-scale
employment of something is its use
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Spain stands in the way of mass use of rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubber' looks like the material; it means a person who rubs. E for Spain comes from international car registration plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseuse gives massages, kneading and stroking clients, so she is one who rubs.

clue.text: Proved last month this writer's about to pen study

indicators.note: a pen encloses animals, so one piece encloses another
turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: December, the last month of the year, abbreviated
the setter saying 'I have', contracted
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: A writer claims last month to be about to write a piece that proves something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer' is the setter speaking of themself, a common crossword device; the first two pieces are reversed together before the third goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To evidence a claim is to show it is true by supplying support, so the past forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Watch perhaps number cutting metal, they're periodically visible

indicators.note: a blade cutting into something goes inside it, so one piece is inserted in another

parts.note: chrome is chromium, a metal used in plating
NO is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: something seen only at intervals shows every other letter

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A watch whose numbers, cut into metal, can be seen only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a numeral on a watch face but is the abbreviation, and 'they're' is used purely for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronometer is a very accurate timepiece, and a watch is one example of a timepiece, hence the qualifier.

clue.text: Exemplary type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: serving as a perfect example to copy
second meaning: a version or design of a product, as of a car

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a phrase for a well-behaved person, but they are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means worthy of imitation, as a noun a particular design or version of something manufactured.

clue.text: Following American trend, to a certain extent

parts.note: following means coming after
A is the abbreviation for American
a trend is a fashion

explanation.surface: Someone partly follows an American trend.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one person following a trend; it is three pieces end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means somewhat or in a rough way, not fully or well, so it matches the limiting phrase.

clue.text: Aim to involve nun, not half demanding attention

indicators.note: without half of it, so the word loses its second half
to involve is to take in, so one piece contains another

parts.note: an aim is an intent
a nun is a sister, and half of that word is kept

explanation.surface: A plan to involve a nun who wants attention.
explanation.walkthrough: A nun is addressed as Sister, and halving that title leaves the piece that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistent describes someone who keeps pressing a demand and will not be ignored, matching the adjectival phrase.

clue.text: Times are flexible for airline

indicators.note: something flexible can be bent into other shapes, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An airline offers flexible departure times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' sounds like a selling point for flight times; it rearranges TIMES ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emirates is the international airline based in Dubai, so it is a named example of the category.

clue.text: Married Lois in Israel, amazingly wealthy lady

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married

indicators.note: something amazing is astonishing and out of the ordinary, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Lois got married in Israel and amazingly turned out to be a very rich woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the letters to rearrange, after M for married.
explanation.definitionFit: A millionairess is a woman worth over a million, which is a precise form of a rich woman.

clue.text: Whole of Bury for instance to visit

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's home, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: The whole town of Bury, a place in Greater Manchester, is to have visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the English town; here it is the verb, INTER. 'Whole' works as a noun, a whole thing or whole number.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, and in older usage any complete entity or whole, so the noun senses coincide.

clue.text: Broadcast about England cricketer on the way

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard over the air, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: about can mean on, concerning a subject
Joe Root is a leading England batsman

explanation.surface: A radio commentary about an England cricketer travelling to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: ON ROOT, said aloud, gives the French-derived phrase, with ROUTE pronounced 'root' in British English. Joe Root is a former England Test captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed French phrase means in the course of a journey, so it is an exact synonym.

clue.text: Train conks out — closure of Circle Line!

parts.note: a machine that conks out stops working, or dies

indicators.note: the closure of something is its end, so only the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A train breaks down, shutting London's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; the capitals are surface dressing, and 'Train' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a locomotive or train driven by a diesel engine, a common shorthand in railway talk.

clue.text: Genuine lamp changing hands

indicators.note: each hand has a one-letter abbreviation, so the letter standing for one hand is exchanged for the other's

parts.note: a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: A real antique lamp is sold to a new owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' suggests a sale, but means swapping L (left) for R (right) in LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Right can mean proper or authentic, as in the right stuff, matching genuine as an adjective.

clue.text: Person with a stable job?

parts.note: surface reading: someone in secure, steady employment
setter's reading: work done in a stable, looking after horses

explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' means secure in the surface, but it is a building for horses, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom is employed to care for horses, feeding and brushing them, so the work is literally in a stable.

clue.text: Retired actor meets a PM and Hindu teacher

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor
taken as written
Rishi Sunak was the UK Prime Minister from 2022 to 2024

explanation.surface: A retired actor meets a Prime Minister and a guru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reads as no longer working; it turns HAM round. The PM is named by his first name, Rishi.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu sage or spiritual guide, literally a great seer, so a teacher in that faith.

clue.text: Allowing vacuous teenagers to give opinions

parts.note: allowing that, or granting, can mean though

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied and only its outside letters kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Letting empty-headed teenagers have their say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' looks like an insult to teenagers, but it empties the word, leaving TS. 'Allowing' as a conjunction, granting that, means though.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's thoughts on a subject are their views or opinions, so the plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Where in New York one can see Cats?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the five boroughs of the city
second meaning: female cats, as breeders call them

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the musical Cats on Broadway; the capital C hides plain female cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens is a borough of New York City, and a queen is the term for an adult female cat.

clue.text: Dark gold round hat

parts.note: sombre means dark or gloomy

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A dark hat with a round golden trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the shape of the hat, but it turns the heraldic gold back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat, so it is a specific example of the general headwear term.

clue.text: Type of surgeon, name former Democrat holds back

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the clue names the kind of surgeon it describes, as in dental surgeon

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run backwards
to hold is to keep within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: late can mean former, as in the late chairman
N is the abbreviation for name
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A surgeon is named whom a former Democrat keeps on.
explanation.walkthrough: LATE holds N, D follows, and the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental surgeon works on teeth, so dental is the adjective naming that kind of surgeon.
